function: mmWave MIMO-OFDM channel estimation: a DNN generates initial factors for unrolled CP-ALS, giving a denoised channel and AoA, AoD, delay estimates from noisy pilot data (pp. 1, 6-7)
system: Downlink mmWave MIMO-OFDM: BS ULA with 32 antennas, MS ULA with 8, 128 subcarriers, 4 paths; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 6, 8)
method: Unfolded model-based learning: fully connected DNN (4 hidden layers, 512 neurons) generates initial factors for CP-ALS; unsupervised end-to-end training on noisy data, no clean labels (pp. 4-6, 8)
data_channel: Own simulator: random geometry-based mmWave channel (4 paths; AoA, AoD uniform; delay 0-100 ns; Gaussian gains), 100,000 samples, 90,000 training and 10,000 test (pp. 6, 8)
test_conditions: Trained on 90,000 samples with mixed SNRs 5-25 dB; tested at each SNR on 10,000 held-out samples of the same random channel distribution (p. 8)
baselines: Non-learned: Random-, SVD- and GEVD-initialized CPALS, structured CP subspace method SCPD, MMSE. Learned: supervised CNN SFCNN [37] (channel denoising) (pp. 7-9)
metrics: Normalized square error (ANSE) of channel and of AoA, AoD, delay estimates; CP objective value; iterations needed; flops; running time (pp. 7-10)
complexity: DNN initializer: 1,884,160 flops (314 kilo cflops), 1,886,304 parameters, 0.6 ms per sample; each CPALS iteration 40 kilo cflops; complexity orders in Table III (pp. 8, 10)
openness: none; only third-party links are cited (baseline SFCNN code CNN4CE, THOP, Tensorlab), no code or data of the authors (pp. 7-10)
q1_support: p. 8: "are i.i.d. with distribution". Path AoA, AoD, delay and gains are drawn from uniform and Gaussian laws in the authors' own simulator of the geometry-based model of p. 6; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "randomly for testing and the rest 90.000 samples are used". The test set is a random part of the same generated data; training uses mixed SNRs 5-25 dB and each SNR is tested, a sweep; no new scenario, antenna number, pilot number, band or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 8: "MIMO-OFDM channel estimation method SFCNN [37] is also". SFCNN, a supervised CNN, is the earlier learned baseline; non-learned MMSE, SCPD, Random-CPALS and SVD-CPALS are compared with it on the channel ANSE in Fig. 7 (p. 9).
q4_support: p. 10: "the DNN model of the proposed DL-CPALS requires 1884160". Flops (about 314 kilo cflops, Table III with complexity orders), 1,886,304 parameters (p. 8) and about 0.6 ms of initialization time per sample (p. 10) are reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "Other settings are the same as in the opensource codes of the paper". The only code link is the baseline SFCNN repository (footnote 4); the paper releases no code or data of its own and uses simulated channels.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v2 (20 Nov 2024) of the DL-CPALS paper; the text does not print the DOI, so the match rests on the title and topic. Area 2: the DNN-aided CP-ALS estimates the MIMO-OFDM channel and its path parameters; the generic synthetic CP decomposition of Section VI-A is not graded. q2: K = 2 iterations in training and K = 50 in testing is an algorithm setting, not a new scenario. The carrier frequency is never stated.
